reports.title: Upper Iowa River (above Decorah) fishing report
reports.text: Smallmouth Bass – Fair: Try fishing the rock ledges or eddies.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Viking Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Black Crappie – Slow: Look for crappies around deep tree piles. Fish will average 9-inches. There is a large year class of 6-inch black crappie in the lake.
Largemouth Bass – Fair: Cast the shoreline just outside the flooded terrestrial vegetation. Anglers are catching numbers of bass in shallow tree piles.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Volga Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Black Crappie - Fair: Slowly troll or paddle deeper water; use a spinner bait.
Largemouth Bass – Fair: Find bass around fish attracting structures. Area interior rivers and streams are low. Clarity is good on most area rivers and streams. Temperatures in the low 80s during the day to 50s overnight. Possibility of scattered thunderstorms through the weekend. For current fishing information, please call the Chuck Gipp Decorah Fish Hatchery at 563-382-8324.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Beeds Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Black Crappie – Good: Try drift fishing or troll tube jigs along the north shore.
Largemouth Bass – Fair.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Big Hollow Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Black Crappie – Slow: Crappies remain in 6 feet of water in the flooded timber. Vertical jigging works best. Slip bobber and minnows are also picking up a few fish.
Largemouth Bass – Slow: Look for bass down at about 6 feet, no deeper. Flip soft plastics and jigs back into the flooded timber at 4-6 feet down to find them.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Brinker Lake fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth Bass – Good: Try early morning or late evening topwater artificial baits.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Cedar River (above Nashua) fishing report
reports.text:
Black Crappie – Fair: Find crappie in brush piles or around woody structure. Use a minnow under a bobber.
Smallmouth Bass - Good: Use a jig with natural colored twister tail or nightcrawler in the brush piles.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Clear Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Black Crappie – Fair: Find suspended fish with your electronics.
Largemouth Bass – Fair.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: George Wyth Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Anglers have been fishing for largemouth bass and panfish. Some sorting is needed for bluegill and crappie.
Black Crappie – Fair: Locate structure using electronics and jig colored tube jigs at various depths to find fish.
Largemouth Bass – Fair: Try early morning or late evening top water artificial baits.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Green Valley Lake fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth Bass – Slow: Catch largemouth bass up to 20-inches with finesse plastics fished along deep cedar tree brush piles early morning or late evening.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Iowa Lake (Iowa Co.) fishing report
reports.text:
Black Crappie – Fair: Use minnows fished 4-8 down over deeper water. Some sorting is needed; 8-inch and 10-inch fish are being caught.
Largemouth Bass – Good: Try fishing around remaining weeds or laydowns. Most fish are 1-2 pounds.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Kent Park Lake fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth Bass – Fair: Try fishing the outside weedline with plastics or on top with frogs.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Lake Belva Deer fishing report
reports.text:
Black Crappie - Slow: A few anglers early in the morning are still picking up a few in about 6 to 7 feet along the trees out from the beach.
Largemouth Bass – Slow: Bass are suspended down about 6-7 feet out in the trees. Try soft plastic or weedless jigs early in the morning.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Lake Darling fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth Bass – Slow: Water is fairly clear below the phytoplankton layer (about 2.5 feet). Run a shallow diving crankbait (0-4 feet) just below that in the morning or a medium diver (5-9 feet) trolled a little later in the day.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Lake Hendricks fishing report
reports.text:
Black Crappie - Fair: Use a spinner or crankbait pulled slowly behind a small watercraft. Crappie are suspended throughout lake.
Largemouth Bass – Fair: Try a topwater or weedless lure along weed edges.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Lake Meyer fishing report
reports.text:
Black Crappie – Fair: Crappies are suspended. Try trolling around the lake with a spinner or jig tipped with a light colored plastic tail.
Largemouth Bass – Fair: Try a topwater lure along the weed edges.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Lost Grove Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Black Crappie – Slow: Crappies are out along the edge of the flooded timber in 8 to 10 feet of water. Try vertical jigging or slow trolling until you find them.
Largemouth Bass – Slow: Try vertically jigging in or along the outer edge of the flooded timber in 10-12 feet of water. Water temperature down there is about 5 to 6 degrees cooler. Weedless rigged soft plastics can help you keep out of the snags.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Mississippi River Pool 14 fishing report
reports.text:
Largemouth Bass – Excellent: Bass fishing is good along boat ramp areas and newly exposed flooded vegetation lines. Try soft plastics along vegetation lines and brush piles.
Smallmouth Bass – Good: Cast inline spinners just off rock points to catch smallmouth feeding in the rocks; exposed wing-dam rock can be very good.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Prairie Rose Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Black Crappie – Slow: Look for crappie around deep tree piles; fish average 10-inches.
Largemouth Bass – Good: Largemouth bass can be caught all around the lake.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Rice Lake fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth Bass – Good: Bass are biting on a variety of baits.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Turkey River (above Clermont) fishing report
reports.text: Smallmouth Bass – Fair: Try fishing the rock ledges or back eddies.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Twelve Mile Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Black Crappie – Slow: Use a jig tipped with a minnow along the road bed or rockpiles to catch black crappie of all sizes.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Upper Iowa River (above Decorah) fishing report
reports.text: Smallmouth Bass – Fair: Try fishing the rock ledges or eddies. Walleye – Fair: Use a jig tipped with plastic tail or crankbait in deeper pools later in the day or early morning.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Upper Iowa River (below Decorah) fishing report
reports.text: Smallmouth Bass – Fair: Use a jig tipped with a crawler or crawdad in the deeper pools or around rock ledges. A bright colored crankbait also works.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Volga Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Black Crappie - Fair: Slowly troll or paddle deeper water; use a spinner bait.
Largemouth Bass – Fair: Find bass around fish attracting structures. Area interior rivers and streams are low. Clarity is good on most area rivers and streams. Temperatures in the 80s during the day to 60s overnight. Possibility of scattered thunderstorms through the weekend. For current fishing information, please call the Chuck Gipp Decorah Fish Hatchery at 563-382-8324.
